item.title: Bloomington residents asked to save water during drought
item.description: The City of Bloomington is continuing to experience a severe drought, with both lakes dropping four more inches combined since Friday, and the city is asking residents to help reduce water usage by ten percent.

item.title: Shootin' the Breeze | EP. 101: Worsening drought and funny super bowl commercials
item.description: The Storm Prediction Center has released a new outlook map categorizing significant weather, while an EF-1 tornado caused minor damage in Marshall and Putnam counties in February 2024, and the Big Game brought some funny commercials.

item.title: Town of Normal facilities earns top ISSA certification
item.description: The Town of Normal Facilities Department earned a high honor from the ISSA for providing a clean, safe and welcoming environment, and was only the second municipality in the country to receive the CIMS-Green Building Certification with Honors.

item.title: New river otter arrives at Wildlife Prairie Park
item.description: Thatcher, a 7-year-old river otter, has successfully adjusted to her new environment at Wildlife Prairie Park, where she is building bonds with her keepers and showing off her curious personality.

item.title: Free Valentine's cabaret in Peoria supports local food bank
item.description: The Westminster Community Center in Peoria is hosting a free cabaret event, "Curses or Kisses: Love Me or Leave Me", with an Italian buffet and interactive elements to raise donations for the Westminster Food Bank.

item.title: Central Illinois drought worsens, little relief in sight
item.description: Peoria, Ill. (WMBD) -- Thursday's drought monitor report continued to show worsening drought conditions across central Illinois. Much of the area is now in a moderate or severe drought and there is little relief on the way, at least for now. item.title: Most Peoria restaurants fully booked for Valentine's Day Saturday
item.description: Due to Valentine's Day falling on a Saturday, restaurants in the Peoria area are booked solid for dinner reservations, and people who have not yet made a reservation may need to consider other days or options.

item.title: New bill aims to prevent kids' accidental cannabis intake
item.description: A state bill has been proposed to require new signage on marijuana products to warn buyers to keep them out of reach of children and in locked containers, in order to reduce accidental consumption by kids.

item.title: Par-A-Dice redevelopment hearing postponed due to plan change
item.description: The hearing for the Par-A-Dice redevelopment project in Cook County was cancelled due to a change in the plan, and the city of Peoria and Boyd Gaming will now meet on February 18 for a status hearing.

item.title: Honoring Black History: Mental health care barriers for African Americans
item.description: African American adults are 11% less likely to report having a mental illness and 36% less likely to have received mental health treatment, due to a lack of resources, distrust of the medical community, and socioeconomic factors such as poverty and lack of insurance.
